note: Committed route geometry for cmd/simulate (ADR-008). These are hand-written polylines,
not excerpts from a mapping product: a handful of waypoints along real Bengaluru
corridors, enough for vehicles to move along believable paths and for the viewer to draw
something recognisable. They are deliberately small and reviewable, and they are the
reason the benchmark is reproducible — the same seed and the same file produce the same
positions on any machine, with no network call and no external API.
Coordinates are [lat, lon] pairs in WGS84. Every route is a CLOSED circuit: the last point
repeats the first, so a vehicle that reaches the end continues onto the closing segment
instead of teleporting back across the map. The closing segment is the return leg — a
straight line rather than a road, which is the one piece of fiction in this file and is
stated here rather than left for a reader to notice.
